## 1. What was read

**1,152 research articles** from 32 of the 33 journals on the roster.

A further **442** records (28% of the 1,594 this month's harvest returned) carry no abstract and are not research: news, correspondence, editor highlights and obituaries. PubMed types them `Journal Article` and nothing else, so the publication-type filter cannot see them — across the whole index they are 22.7% of it and 35% of `general`, and 3,801 of them are JAMA. Every count below is over the full harvest and is inflated by this; the figure above is not.

| General | Cancer | Immune | Bioinfo | Sysbio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 737 | 280 | 109 | 418 | 50 |

!!! warning "Volume swing against the median month: bioinfo +54%, cancer +51%, general +57%, immune +30%, sysbio +108%"
    Check the source before reading anything into this. Two benign causes account for most of these. `bioinfo` every January carries the Nucleic Acids Research database issue and runs high. And several journals simply deposit nothing in some months: across the 44 months read, 4 of 33 journals are absent from at least one, worst being *Nat Mach Intell* (20 months missing, 81 papers in total) and *Bioinformatics* (4 months missing, 2,905 papers in total). This month is missing *Nat Mach Intell*. Queried directly, PubMed returns zero for those journal-months too — the holes are in the source, reproduced exactly by re-running the harvest. So a swing here is not evidence that a field went quiet, and is not usually evidence that the pipeline broke either.

Largest contributors: JAMA 232, Bioinformatics 173, Nature 157, Science 84, Blood 78, Nat Med 75.

## 3. The evidence that moved it





**A universal cell embedding, one month after the scaling nulls.**
[42420460](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42420460/) (*Nature*): universal cell embedding as a foundation model for
cell biology. July 2026 carried two independent findings that neither size nor
diversity of the pretraining set buys single-cell foundation-model performance,
one of them titled "much pain with little gain". August publishes a universal
embedding in *Nature* regardless. This is the thread's characteristic shape and
the reason it sits at `splitting` rather than resolving: the negative results are
in the same venues, at the same tier, in adjacent months, and the programme does
not turn.

**Generative AI gets a cluster-randomised trial.** [42362867](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42362867/) (*Nat Med*): a
generative-AI clinical decision support system in primary care, pragmatic and
cluster-randomised. Read against the 2024 backfill, this is the continuation of
a line that starts with a randomised nurse-plus-LLM trial in October 2024
([39009780](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39009780/)) — not, as this corpus argued through 2025, the arrival of
evidence into a vacuum.

**CAR-T's failure modes get specific.** [42270901](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42270901/) (*Nat Cancer*):
iron-mediated ferroptosis **impairs** CAR-T function and antitumour efficacy.
[42296961](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42296961/) (*Cell*): the endogenous immune compartment is critical after
CAR-T in recurrent glioblastoma — the engineered product is not sufficient by
itself. Against those, [42387022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42387022/) takes GPNMB-directed CAR-T into
fusion-driven solid tumours and [42447427](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42447427/) reports phase I TRAVERSE, an
**allogeneic** CD70-targeted product in renal cell carcinoma. Allogeneic and
solid-tumour in one trial is the combination the thread has been waiting on.

**Nerves recruited by epithelium, with the transmitter named.** [42361796](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42361796/)
(*Cell*): excessive epithelial mechanosensation drives nociceptive innervation
and chronic bladder pain via a PIEZO1-SLC7A11-glutamate axis. The direction is
epithelium to nerve, which is the less-reported half of the neuro-immune claim.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

[41997295](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41997295/): DART (NCI/SWOG S1609), comprehensive final results for dual
CTLA-4 and PD-1 blockade in rare cancers. The definitive readout of the
combination strategy in the setting where it had the least competition.

### (b) Method credibility

[42377339](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42377339/) (*JEM*): retraction of an in vivo nucleolin-targeting paper on
breast cancer aggressiveness through miRNA regulation.

**A partial month, and a warning about the ones before it.** August 2026 was
harvested on the 26th and is incomplete; treat every count here as a floor. More
importantly, this is the first briefing written after the corpus's own premise
was measured. Meetings do lead the journals — by about ten to thirteen months,
stable across every matching threshold — but roughly one abstract in a hundred
ever becomes a paper in these journals, and ranking meeting vocabulary predicts
journal growth no better than a random half of the journals' own back-catalogue.
See `clinical-practice` in `data/threads.yml` for the numbers.
